newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwandan refugee group urges U.N. inquiry in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan refugee group urges U.N. inquiry in Zaire.

text.p: A Rwandan Hutu refugee lobby group urged the international community on Thursday to put pressure on Zairean rebels to stop blocking a U.N. investigation of reports Rwandan refugees were being slaughtered in Zaire.
The Rally for the Return of Refugees and Democracy in Rwanda (RDR) said rebels refused to give a U.N. team the assurances necessary for its investigation because they wanted to hide massacres.

"RDR calls on the United Nations, European Union and the Organisation of African Unity to put pressure on the rebels and their Ugandan and Rwandan sponsors to make sure the mission is carried out without any hindrance," RDR said in a statement.
"The mission should not only investigate the massacres but also the disappearance of what is officially estimated at more than 300,000 refugees," the Hutu refugee lobby group added.

The Rwandan government, which has said it supports the rebellion in Zaire by the AFDL, says there are only some 50,000 Rwandan refugees left in eastern Zaire including 20,000 found by aid agencies south of the northeastern capital of Kisangani.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR estimates there are between 200,000 and 300,000 refugees in Zaire, most of them unaccounted for since they fled their camps in the east of the country late last year.
U.N. investigators left Rwanda last Saturday after waiting a week for rebels to give them clearance to start work in eastern Zaire to check reports rebel forces were massacring refugees.
The blockage was a challenge to the United Nations, whose human rights body ordered the mission, and to western nations that condemned the alleged killings and urged the rebels to cooperate.
The Hutu refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 and are collectively accused by minority Tutsis of genocide in Rwanda the same year.
